assertions.description: The WebTransport constructor exists (datagramsReadableType extends its options dictionary).
The constructor converts the datagramsReadableType dictionary member (observed via a throwing getter, not inferred).
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; let read = false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { get datagramsReadableType() { read = true; return undefined; } }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); try { t.close(); } catch {} } catch {} return read; })()

assertions.description: Constructing with datagramsReadableType: "bytes" makes datagrams.readable a readable byte stream: getReader({ mode: "byob" }) returns a ReadableStreamBYOBReader.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { datagramsReadableType: 'bytes' }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); try { const r = t.datagrams.readable.getReader({ mode: 'byob' }); const ok = r.constructor.name === 'ReadableStreamBYOBReader'; r.releaseLock(); try { t.close(); } catch {} return ok; } catch { try { t.close(); } catch {} return false; } } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: With the option absent, datagrams.readable is a DEFAULT readable stream, so getReader({ mode: "byob" }) throws a TypeError. (Legacy Chromium builds fail this: their datagram readable was always a byte stream — the state this feature replaces.)
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never'); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); let threw = false; try { t.datagrams.readable.getReader({ mode: 'byob' }).releaseLock(); } catch (e) { threw = e instanceof TypeError; } try { t.close(); } catch {} return threw; } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: Whatever the option, a default reader on datagrams.readable is always obtainable — the opt-in may add BYOB, it never removes default reading.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { datagramsReadableType: 'bytes' }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); try { const r = t.datagrams.readable.getReader(); const ok = r.constructor.name === 'ReadableStreamDefaultReader'; r.releaseLock(); try { t.close(); } catch {} return ok; } catch { try { t.close(); } catch {} return false; } } catch { return false; } })()

assertions.description: datagramsReadableType is typed as the ReadableStreamType enum ("bytes" only), so a build that reads the member must throw TypeError for any other string.
assertions.test: (() => { if (typeof WebTransport !== 'function') return false; let read = false; try { new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { get datagramsReadableType() { read = true; return undefined; } }); } catch {} if (!read) return false; try { const t = new WebTransport('https://127.0.0.1:44443/never', { datagramsReadableType: 'not-a-real-type' }); t.ready.catch(() => {}); t.closed.catch(() => {}); try { t.close(); } catch {} return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: On a live session constructed without the option, a received empty datagram is delivered as a zero-length chunk (byte streams cannot represent it). Needs real datagram traffic, which requires an HTTP/3 endpoint this showcase cannot reach.
assertions.test: Requires a live HTTP/3 WebTransport server sending a zero-length datagram.
